recorded.values: INVENTED. Every situation below is synthetic. R1 SL-4's Definition of Done requires an eval/scenario set with the S2 §15 rationale rubric for next-work choice; it does not require pilot-derived situations, and a shadow Slice has no organic corpus of multi-day supervisor decisions to harvest. The shapes are modelled on S2 §8.2 (the decision sequence), §8.3 (work discovery), §8.5 (learn before acting), §8.13 (commitments), §8.17 (diminishing returns), §8.19 (waiting as a strategy), the AC-01…AC-04 acceptance scenarios in scope for this Slice, and the edge cases EC-01, EC-20, EC-23, EC-25, EC-26, EC-29, EC-30 and EC-40. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced here.
recorded.gap: This set is wholly synthetic, which is a real limitation and is stated rather than hidden: it measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities. It also cannot measure multi-day coherence — a single-turn eval sees one situation at a time, and posture-history coherence across days is RS-2 hosted evidence (SA-4.3), not something a fixture can produce. Pilot-derived situations would enter the same way SL-2's real openings did: captured under an explicit bounded authorization, redacted, and labelled by human review independently of the model's own output, with what the model said never copied into the expectation.
recorded.barEstablishedBy: PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT on 2026-09-08, BEFORE this set was run even once, per Methodology §14.1 and the SL-4 Definition of Done — not by a human, and with no human approval sought or given at that point. Methodology §14.1 requires that a MATERIAL product/risk threshold be reviewed and RATIFIED by the appropriate human authority before it can be used to CLOSE the governed Slice. That ratification has NOT happened yet. Until it does, this bar is the agent's frozen proposal and nothing here may be read as human-accepted risk.
recorded.whyTheseTwoBars: The two error directions are not equally costly, so they are not pooled. `failure_rate_bar` measures ordinary semantic accuracy: choosing a defensible posture for the situation. `fabricated_work_bar` is ZERO and measures the one failure this Slice exists to detect — manufacturing activity, a commitment, or confident work that the evidence does not support. S2's whole quality bar is built around deliberate no-op being a correct answer and quiet not being broken; a supervisor that invents work to look busy fails the Slice however accurate its other judgments are.
recorded.runHistory: RECORDED IN FULL, INCLUDING THE FAILURES, because a tidied history would hide the only thing that made this evidence worth anything. FIRST RUN (2026-09-08) BREACHED BOTH BARS: 8/16 failures (50%) against a 20% bar, and 2 fabrications against a bar of 0. The bars were NOT moved and not one expected label was changed at any point. What changed was the implementation and, once, the verifier. REPAIR 1 — THE PROMPT WAS UNDER-SPECIFIED AGAINST S2. Five governing rules the set legitimately tests were simply absent from it, and the model failed exactly those scenarios: that unavailable CONTACT does not make internal work worthless (§8.1 invariant 5, AC-03) — the model twice read 'cannot message' as 'nothing to do'; that a DUE commitment is a reason to do the work rather than to wait (§8.13, §8.15); that a technical work failure is not a commercial signal (EC-15, EC-33, AC-48); that a materially new commercial objective goes to a human instead of being absorbed (invariant 38, EC-30, AC-46); and that only LISTED capabilities may be used (invariant 36, EC-25, AC-37). The normalizer's shape constraint was also unstated, which is why one scenario produced no usable judgment at all. REPAIR 2 — THE VERIFIER CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT FAILURES. Both 'fabrications' in the first run were the model re-listing a commitment the scenario had already given it as tracked. That is REDUNDANCY, not invention: the promise is real, already recorded, and `recordCommitments` is idempotent on its key, so nothing durable is created twice. The zero bar was written for the opposite thing — a promise the brokerage never made — as `bar_rationale` says in as many words. `must_not_repeat_commitment` now scores redundancy as an ordinary failure; `must_not_detect_commitment` keeps fabrication semantics, which `vague-intention-is-not-a-commitment` continues to police. The bar number did not move. REPAIR 3 — TWO INTERFACE DEFECTS, not prompt wording. The judge was being asked not to duplicate open Work and not to re-list tracked commitments, while being shown NEITHER the open Work's types (only aggregate counts) NOR the tracked commitment keys. It was being asked for judgments it had no basis to make. Both are now supplied, and the capability list is labelled exhaustive. S2 §8.2 asks the context compile for 'open / blocked / recent Work', not counts of it, so this was under-implementing TD-8 rather than tuning. AN ATTEMPT THAT WAS REVERTED AS PHRASED: an absolute 'blocked work is yours to resolve, never no_op' rule fixed the systematic failure but pushed the model toward action generally, and fabrications rose from 0 to 1-2 per run. It was re-phrased to key on work STATUS — `todo` is underway and needs nothing, `blocked`/`failed` is unfinished responsibility — which is what EC-15 and §8.16 actually say. That is the version in the prompt. A DIFFERENT MODEL WAS TRIED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` scored 50% across three runs, mostly by emitting proposals the normalizer had to discard as structurally incoherent. The default `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` stands. FINAL MEASUREMENT: TWO INDEPENDENT BATCHES OF FIVE RUNS EACH — 10 runs total. Both frozen bars held in ALL TEN. Failure rates 6.3%, 12.5%, 18.8%, 12.5%, 12.5% and 12.5%, 18.8%, 12.5%, 6.3%, 6.3%; ZERO fabrications in every run. Measured over repeated runs deliberately: an earlier single passing run was followed by a failing one, and a bar that a judgment crosses one time in three is not held by a single lucky measurement.
recorded.knownWeakness: `work-failed-technically` fails in 10 of 10 runs — the one SYSTEMATIC finding, recorded rather than tuned away. Given a Work Item left `blocked` by a technical failure and a prospect waiting, the supervisor reliably chooses `no_op`. It does NOT do the forbidden thing — it never reads the failure as commercial bad news — but it also does not pick the failure up, which EC-15 and §8.21's stopping conditions ask of it. It sits inside the failure-rate bar, so it does not breach anything; it is a real limit of this model at this prompt and is stated so that nobody reads a passing run as meaning the behavior is uniformly good. `conflicting-availability` and `capability-not-available` fail intermittently (2-4 and 1-3 of 5) — variance rather than a systematic gap.
recorded.repairBarsEstablishedBy: PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT on 2026-09-14, BEFORE the extended set was run even once, for the Cycle 3 repair (Slice Plan §5 order 2, §6): the supervisor now reads a human's answer. Three bars must hold in EVERY run. `failure_rate_bar` 0.2 and `fabricated_work_bar` 0 apply over the whole extended set: they are the values SL-4 froze, RE-PROPOSED here for this repair rather than inherited, because SL-4's human ratification (2026-09-09) was scoped to SL-4's evidence and is not a standing threshold (Methodology §14.1). `reask_bar` 0 is new. In a scenario whose one human-answerable question has already been answered, a targeted ask re-asks what a person already said — the defect this repair exists to remove — so no rate of it is tolerated. The repair is measured over FIVE runs and holds only if all five hold all three bars. These bars are the agent's frozen proposal, not human-accepted risk: the Accountable must RATIFY them before the repair is recorded closed.
recorded.repairScope: The judge's input gained `humanAnswers`. For settled Work carrying a person's answer (`result_jsonb.human_answer`, written by the Work Portfolio), it gives what was asked, who answered by role, when, and what they said — quoted as data and length-bounded. Every existing scenario states `humanAnswers: []`; no existing expectation, label or scoring changed. Two scenarios were added (`covers: answered_human_input`): an answer that unblocks the next work (S2 HP-08), and an answer that changes the plan (S2 §8.5, replan after a human response). A third, an answer asking for a prospect message while contact is unavailable, was considered and deliberately left out. The outbound detector is a keyword match that would score legitimate internal drafting as fabrication, and SA-4.8 already guarantees deterministically that no prospect-facing effect is reachable in shadow.
repairRunHistory: RECORDED IN FULL, INCLUDING THE FAILURES, as SL-4 did.

FIRST RUN of the extended set (2026-09-14; head 3436c72; 5 runs × 18 scenarios; openai/gpt-5.4-mini) BREACHED ALL THREE BARS IN ALL FIVE RUNS: failure rate 27.8, 22.2, 27.8, 27.8 and 22.2%; fabrications 1, 2, 2, 1 and 2; re-asks 1, 0, 1, 0 and 0. The bars were NOT moved, and no expectation or scoring changed.
A SAME-DAY BASELINE separated two causes. It used SL-4's own prompt and original 16 scenarios at af663e5, with the same model.

(1) THE REPAIR REGRESSED EXISTING SITUATIONS. Its answer rule was shown in every prompt. `quiet-nothing-new` then fabricated work in 3 of 5 runs, against 0 of 5 in the baseline, and `attention-already-consumed` in 3 of 5, against 1 of 5. REPAIR: the rule and the answers section now appear only when there is an answer, so every scenario without one renders byte-identically to SL-4's prompt (verified for all 16). The rule is reworded from S2 §8.5 and HP-08: an answer settles its question, and the judge decides what the answer now makes useful — the work it unblocks, or a changed plan.

(2) THE BASELINE ITSELF NO LONGER HOLDS SL-4's BARS. Failure rates of 18.8, 18.8, 6.3, 18.8 and 18.8% held, but fabrications of 1, 1, 0, 0 and 0 breached the zero bar in 2 of 5 runs. One was real: `attention-already-consumed` proposed an inventory search where none is warranted. The other was a false positive of the outbound keyword detector: in `contact-me-after-the-twentieth`, an internal `search_inventory` was scored as contact. `conflicting-availability` now fails 5 of 5 (systematic; intermittent, 2–4 of 5, in SL-4). SL-4's final ten runs held both bars in all ten. This drift is pre-existing and independent of the repair, and it is REPORTED to the Accountable rather than absorbed. While the unchanged baseline breaches the frozen fabrication bar, that bar cannot be held over five runs by any change to the answer path.

SECOND RUN (head d9ce566, same model and bars). Fabrications were 0 in all five runs and re-asks 0 in all five. Failure rates were 5.6, 16.7, 5.6, 22.2 and 11.1%, so run 4 BREACHED the 20% bar and 4 of 5 runs held. `answered-visit-window` passed 5 of 5. `answer-changes-the-plan` chose `no_op` in 2 of 5 runs: told the preferred house was sold, the judge saw nothing left to do, missing that the Opportunity's objective still stands. Run 4's breach was three failures in unchanged situations (`unverified-budget-blocks-match`, `conflicting-availability`, `capability-not-available` — the baseline's ordinary variance) plus that one. REPAIR, the last before reporting: the answer rule adds that when an answer rules out what was being pursued, the objective still stands and the useful work is usually the next path toward it (S2 §8.3 and §8.5). This is bounded: whatever the third run shows is reported, not tuned further.

THIRD RUN (head 29658e3; same model and bars), measured in TWO INDEPENDENT BATCHES OF FIVE, as SL-4 measured, because a single passing batch has been followed by a failing one before. ALL THREE BARS HELD IN ALL TEN RUNS. Failure rates were 11.1, 11.1, 11.1, 5.6 and 11.1% in the first batch and 0.0, 16.7, 11.1, 11.1 and 11.1% in the second. Fabrications were 0 and re-asks were 0 in every run. `answered-visit-window` and `answer-changes-the-plan` passed in all ten.

WHAT THE RATIFICATION MUST WEIGH. The bars were frozen before the first run and never moved, and no expectation or scoring changed at any point. But the implementation was repaired twice after observed breaches, and the second repair was prompted by one of the two new scenarios, so the final wording was shaped by this set and the new scenarios are NOT an independent holdout. The guard against regressing the sixteen unchanged situations is structural, not statistical: their prompts are byte-identical to SL-4's. Separately, the same-day baseline breached the zero-fabrication bar in 2 of its 5 runs, while the fifteen later runs of those same byte-identical sixteen prompts had none. That puts SL-4's zero bar at the edge of this model's variance rather than reliably held — an observation about SL-4's evidence, reported to the Accountable and not absorbed here.
recorded.repairBarsRatifiedBy: RATIFIED by Alejandro Torres Padilla, the Accountable, on 2026-09-14 (−06:00) — AFTER the runs recorded in `repairRunHistory`, and after reviewing that evidence and its caveats. The ratification is scoped to this repair and its current shadow evidence: `failure_rate_bar` 0.2, `fabricated_work_bar` 0, `reask_bar` 0. The sequence, exactly as it occurred: (1) the bars were PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT before the first extended run (commit 94c5636); (2) the implementation was repaired after observed breaches (d9ce566, 29658e3), and the bars never moved; (3) the Accountable ratified them afterwards. This is not a prior human approval, and it does not become a standing threshold for later Slices, the assisted or live stages, or production (Methodology §14.1).
recorded.sl4BaselineVarianceFinding: A MODEL-VARIANCE FINDING about SL-4's evidence, recorded on the Accountable's decision of 2026-09-14. On 2026-09-14, SL-4's own prompt and 16 scenarios (af663e5, openai/gpt-5.4-mini) breached SL-4's zero-fabrication bar in 2 of 5 runs; SL-4's final ten runs had held it in all ten. The bar is NOT changed or relaxed. The observed REAL fabrication — `attention-already-consumed` proposing an inventory search where no work is warranted — stands as observed and is not reinterpreted, and the historical run is not rewritten. The keyword detector's flag on `contact-me-after-the-twentieth` is not a reason to loosen the threshold or rewrite that run. If the detector is later shown to be semantically wrong, that is a SEPARATE verifier defect, repaired only with evidence that preserves the underlying fabrication contract.
recorded.sl14ScenariosFrozen: FROZEN 2026-09-15, BEFORE THE JUDGE WAS TOUCHED (SL-14 ordering constraint 2). Seven scenarios were added for technically blocked Work: a transient failure worth retrying; the same failure after a Supervisor retry; a capability that is gone; a need a person already met; a replan with another capability; Work blocked on a person, which is not technical; and Work that succeeded with a commercially negative result. The SL-4 scenario `work-failed-technically` keeps its acceptable postures and now carries the compile shape SL-14 introduces, plus its recovery expectations. A holdout of six scenarios, sharing no id and no situation with this set, was frozen at the same time in supervisor-holdout-scenarios.json and is run only after the implementation is final.
sl14RunHistory: RECORDED IN FULL, INCLUDING THE FAILURES, as SL-4 and the Cycle 3 repair did. The five bars were frozen on 2026-09-15 before any implementation branch existed and ratified the same day; NOT ONE was moved, and no scenario, expectation, label or acceptable set changed at any point. What changed was the implementation.

FIRST RUN (2026-09-15; 25 scenarios x 5; openai/gpt-5.4-mini) BREACHED IN ALL FIVE: failure rate 28, 28, 32, 40, 32%; 13 of 125 judgments discarded; stranded 1, 1, 1, 1, 2. Three defects, all in the contract SL-14 itself had just added. (1) A RETRY HAD NO COHERENT SHAPE: `proposed_work` was required for every non-quiet posture, but a retry proposes nothing new, so judgments that tried to express one were discarded as incoherent. (2) THE JUDGE NAMED WORK TYPES, NOT ALIASES: the alias was explained only in a schema comment the model never sees. (3) STRANDED WORK: nothing required a disposition per alias.
SECOND RUN: 12-32%; stranded down to 0-1; 6 discards; the first blind retries appeared.

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT FOUND THE REST. A discarded judgment now says WHY, because a silent null makes 'no judgment' indistinguishable from an unreachable model, which is the ambiguity AGENTS section 7 forbids. It immediately disproved the assumed cause of the third run's 14 discards: the model was putting `leave` in `posture`. SL-14's own rule - 'your posture must match what you said in recovery' - had conflated two vocabularies. They are now stated as separate questions.
FOURTH RUN: 20, 8, 16, 20, 16%; fabrications 0; re-asks 0; stranded 0; discards 1; 4 of 5 held. One blind retry breached its zero bar.

TWO MORE IMPLEMENTATION REPAIRS, neither keyed to a scenario. (a) `resolveRecoveryAlias`: the Work line shows both an alias and a work type and the judge sometimes named the type, which was being read as 'no decision' and recorded as stranded when the judge had in fact disposed of the Work - a misreport of the very thing `stranded_failure_bar` measures. Tolerance is confined to WHICH Work was meant; every authority guard still runs on the resolved item, and nothing ambiguous resolves. (b) A retry reason must name what is DIFFERENT NOW from the last attempt, with the already-recurred check moved ahead of the case for retrying (S2 section 8.17).

AN ATTEMPT THAT WAS REVERTED ON EVIDENCE, as SL-4 reverted one: consolidating the posture/recovery coupling into fewer, sharper bullets removed the `work-failed-technically` failure entirely but pushed the model toward action, and blind retries returned in 2 of 5 runs. The version with zero blind retries across ten runs was kept. This is the same seesaw SL-4 recorded, and it is why prompt iteration stopped here.

A MODEL WAS MEASURED AND THE RESULT DISCARDED AS UNINFORMATIVE. `anthropic/claude-opus-5` was run against the holdout to test whether the residual failures are prompt-bound or model-bound. 17 of 30 answers were lost - ALL of them truncation at `max_tokens` 700, none a judgment failure - so it says nothing about that model and is NOT evidence for or against changing the default, which is unchanged. The budget was raised to 1200 because SL-14's own `recovery` field lengthened the answer.

FINAL MEASUREMENT, all from one code state (1ee4699), TWO INDEPENDENT BATCHES OF FIVE on each set. MAIN SET: 4 of 5 and 4 of 5 runs held every bar. Failure rates 16.0, 16.0, 12.0, 12.0, 12.0% and 16.0, 16.0, 8.0, 24.0, 16.0%. Blind retries 0, stranded 0 and re-asks 0 in ALL TEN. The two breaches were one run at 24% and one fabrication flag in each batch. HOLDOUT: 2 of 5 and 2 of 5 held. Failure rates 50.0, 16.7, 16.7, 33.3, 33.3% and 50.0, 33.3, 16.7, 16.7, 50.0%. Fabrications, re-asks and stranded were 0 in all ten; blind retries were 1 in 2 of the 10 runs.

THE DEFINITION OF DONE IS NOT MET, and that is reported rather than absorbed. It requires every run to hold every bar on both sets. On the holdout, 4 of 10 runs did. This is escalated to the Accountable under Methodology section 14.1: the bars are ratified, they are not moved, and an unmet acceptance threshold is not ordinary engineering authority.

WHAT THE HOLDOUT'S NUMBERS DO AND DO NOT MEAN. It has six scenarios, so one failure is 16.7% and two are 33.3%: against a 20% bar it tolerates AT MOST ONE failure per run. That severity is a property of the set size frozen on 2026-09-15, not a measured degradation. The gap from the main set is nonetheless real and is what a holdout is for - the main set's prompt was repaired against its own failures and the holdout's never was, and no prompt change was ever made after seeing a holdout result.

WHAT THE BLIND RETRIES DO AND DO NOT MEAN. The bar counts three situations: the same failure recurred after a Supervisor retry, the capability is gone, or the need is gone. The executor refuses the FIRST TWO deterministically, whatever the judge says - the retry bound and the capability check, both mutation-tested - so in the running system those two cannot happen. Only 'the need is gone' rests on judgment alone. The eval measures the judge, correctly; the system's guarantee is stronger than this number suggests, and both facts belong in the ratification.
recorded.sl14KnownWeakness: `work-succeeded-with-negative-discovery` fails 3-5 of 5 - the clearest SYSTEMATIC finding, recorded rather than tuned away. Work that SUCCEEDED technically and found the property sold is not a technical failure, and the judge correctly never offers to retry it (SA-14.9 holds). It then answers `no_op`, missing that the objective still stands. It cannot be repaired here: its Work list carries no blocked item, so its prompt is byte-identical to SL-4's, and SA-14.1 requires that it stay so. The same shape appears in `work-failed-technically` and the holdout's `h-succeeded-but-unfavourable`. `conflicting-availability` and `capability-not-available` continue to fail intermittently on byte-identical prompts, as SL-4 and the Cycle 3 repair both recorded.
recorded.sl14DetectorFinding: A SECOND AND THIRD INSTANCE OF THE OUTBOUND DETECTOR'S FALSE POSITIVE, recorded under the Accountable's 2026-09-14 ruling that a detector defect is a SEPARATE verifier defect. In the final main-set batches, `contact-me-after-the-twentieth` was flagged for `inventory_screen` and `new-relevant-value-exists` for `prepare_comparison` - both internal work, each with a rationale saying in as many words that it advances the decision WITHOUT contacting the prospect. Those two flags are the ONLY thing separating those two runs from holding every bar. The detector was NOT changed during this measurement: repairing scoring mid-measurement, in the direction that improves the result, is exactly what the discipline forbids. It is proposed as a bounded repair of its own, with the fabrication contract preserved. The artifact should also record WHAT the detector fired on; today it records only that it fired.
recorded.sl14ScenarioFidelityRepair: PROSPECTIVE VERIFIER-FIDELITY REPAIR, 2026-09-16, recorded before the runs that use it. A fidelity audit of every Work line in both sets against the shapes `compileWork` can actually emit found THREE lines the implementation cannot produce - each appending a result narrative to a Work line, a channel the compile does not have. Two are in this set and are repaired here; the third is in the frozen holdout and is NOT touched, because that holdout and its results are kept permanently as recorded evidence. WHAT CHANGED: only the SITUATION, toward what the system really produces. `work-succeeded-with-negative-discovery` had ["inventory_search — done (agent_proposed): la propiedad ya se vendió"] and now has ["inventory_search — done (agent_proposed)"], with the discovery moved to `currentFacts` as `property.availability`, which is where a settled Work result actually lands. `blocked-waiting-on-a-person-not-technical` had ["confirm_budget — blocked (human): esperando la respuesta de una persona"] and now renders its blocked_reason and attempts as the compile does. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: not one expectation, acceptable posture, acceptable recovery, `not_recoverable`, alias list, bar or scoring rule. WHY THIS IS NOT TUNING TO A RESULT: the repair is justified by the implementation, not by the numbers - a situation the system cannot produce is a situation the eval must not score. The evidence that the posture failure it was producing is NOT SL-14's is separate and direct: under the PRE-SL-14 judge, on a prompt SA-14.1 requires to stay byte-identical, `work-succeeded-with-negative-discovery` failed 5 of 5 with `no_op` every time. SL-14 is structurally unable to affect it. Its SL-14 claim, SA-14.9, is carried by `not_recoverable` and the empty alias list, and held in 10 of 10 runs before this repair. THE ORIGINAL Q10 EVIDENCE IS PRESERVED EXACTLY and no historical run becomes a pass retroactively.

bar_rationale: 0.2 mirrors the overall semantic bar SL-3 froze for a task of the same class (short situational judgment with strict JSON output), and is deliberately not tightened on the strength of SL-3's observed results — a bar borrowed from another Slice's OUTCOME would be a bar set by evidence rather than before it. This set is harder than SL-3's: several scenarios have more than one defensible posture, which is exactly what S2 AC-31 says ('selection explainable via current context; no universal score required'), so scoring accepts any listed posture and judges the rationale against the scenario's rubric. `fabricated_work_bar` is 0 because there is no acceptable rate of manufactured work: EC-20 and EC-40 make deliberate quiescence a correct outcome, and one fabricated commitment silently misrepresents a promise the brokerage never made. SL-14 adds two zero bars for the two failure directions the Accountable named on 2026-09-15, ratified the same day for SL-14's RS-2 scope: `blind_retry_bar` counts a retry of technically blocked Work where the evidence says a retry cannot help — the failure treated as an order to retry (S2 §8.17) — and `stranded_failure_bar` counts technically blocked Work left with no coherent disposition, which is what SL-4's evidence showed (S2 §8.21). Neither loosens the SL-4 or Cycle 3 bars, which are unchanged.
